anvilsolver.configuration.title: Anvil Solver
anvilsolver.configuration.section.anvils: Every Anvil Solver option. These are client-only and are stored in config/anvilsolver-client.toml.
anvilsolver.configuration.enabled.toolti: Show the anvil solver overlay in the TFC anvil screen.
anvilsolver.configuration.highlightNextB: Draw a bright outline over the anvil's own step button for the next press, so you can click that button directly instead of reading the step off the overlay list. Only shown while a solution exists and at least one press is still needed, and hidden while the item is too cold to work.
anvilsolver.configuration.showTemperatur: Add one line with the item's current temperature and a bar showing it against the temperature the item must reach before presses register, plus a rough countdown while it is cooling. This controls that line only: the too-cold warning still appears when it is off. No effect on items that cannot be heated.
anvilsolver.configuration.showAlloyCalcu: Show the alloy calculator overlay in the TFC crucible screen. Lists what is in the crucible as a percentage of the total, names the alloy it currently makes, and works out the fewest whole ingots to melt in to reach a target alloy. The overlay also lists the alloys you can still reach: click one to target it, or click 'Auto' to go back to letting the mod choose. Auto picks the alloy that needs the fewest ingots to finish - that is what 'closest' means here, rather than whichever alloy the mix already resembles - and any alloy it cannot find a mix for is listed last. The list shows up to eight at a time, fewer if the game window is too short: scroll the mouse wheel over the box to reach the rest, or use the 'Cycle alloy target' key (default G) to step through them from the keyboard. Only alloys containing everything already in the pot are offered, since metal cannot be taken back out - an empty crucible can reach any of them. Every ingot count in one list is part of the same plan: melt them all in and the mix lands in range. Independent of the 'Show overlay' option, which governs the anvil overlay only.
Also show raw ore counts under each metal in the alloy calculator - one short line such as 'ore: 53P / 32N / 23R', giving the whole poor, normal and rich ore to melt in instead of ingots. Early on you are usually melting ore straight into the crucible rather than making ingots first, so an answer in ingots alone is the wrong unit for that part of the game. The three figures are alternatives, not parts of one plan: 53 poor ore OR 32 normal OR 23 rich. Each is solved in whole ore of that grade by the same search that produces the ingot counts, so any one of them lands the mix in range on its own - they are not the ingot count divided by an ore's yield, which would round and could overshoot. Ore yields are detected from your own pack's heating recipes, exactly as ingot volumes are, so a datapack or addon that changes them is followed automatically. A grade is left out whenever it cannot be answered without guessing: no ore of that grade for one of the alloy's metals, the metals' yields for that grade disagreeing, or no whole-ore mix existing at all. If none of the three can be answered the line is not drawn - a missing line means 'not known', never a wrong number. A '*' after a figure means your pack's own ore types disagreed on that grade's yield and the commonest value was used; TFC itself never does this. Turn this off to keep the box shorter: on a short game window the extra lines come out of the space the target list would otherwise use.
anvilsolver.configuration.ingotVolume.to: Fallback volume of one metal ingot in mB, used by the alloy calculator to answer in whole ingots instead of raw millibuckets. This is not normally used: the calculator detects each metal's ingot volume from your own pack, by reading the heating recipe that melts that metal's ingot - the same data the game itself uses - so a datapack or addon that changes ingot volumes is followed automatically. This value applies only where that detection cannot answer: no ingot item for the metal, no heating recipe for it, or a recipe that melts into a different metal than expected. 100 is TFC's standard ingot volume and is the right fallback for almost every pack. Detected values are cached per world and refreshed when you change worlds.
anvilsolver.configuration.overlayGap.too: Horizontal gap in pixels between the anvil GUI's right edge and the overlay box. Negative values pull the overlay back over the GUI itself. If the box will not fit on the right it is mirrored to the left of the GUI and this gap is applied on that side instead.
anvilsolver.configuration.overlayY.toolt: Vertical offset in pixels from the anvil GUI's top edge. 0 aligns the top of the overlay box with the top of the GUI panel.
anvilsolver.configuration.maxPresses.too: Maximum number of upcoming presses to list at once.
anvilsolver.configuration.theme.tooltip: Colour theme for the overlay. Affects colours only - never layout or behaviour. TFC Green is the original green-on-black palette. Colourblind safe uses blue for the next press and amber for warnings, so neither relies on telling red from green. High contrast is white text on a more opaque black box. Monochrome uses no colour at all: the next press is simply the brightest line.
